extra_vocab.en: a person who makes a phone call
extra_vocab.note: 多益電話對話、客服與語音留言中很常見，指打進來的人。常和 hold、transfer、call back 等動作一起出現。

example.en: Callers must give their names before the call is transferred.
example.zh: 來電者必須先說出姓名，電話才會被轉接。

example.en: The caller ID showed a number we did not know.
example.zh: 來電顯示出一個我們不認識的號碼。

example.en: Do not give personal data to an unknown caller.
example.zh: 不要把個人資料給不明來電者。

example.en: She put the caller on hold and checked the file.
example.zh: 她讓來電者在線上等候，並查了檔案。

examples.en: The caller asked to speak with someone in the sales department.
examples.zh: 來電者要求和業務部的人說話。

examples.en: A caller left a message about the delayed delivery.
examples.zh: 有位來電者留言詢問延遲的出貨。

examples.en: The receptionist asked the caller to hold for a moment.
examples.zh: 接待人員請來電者稍等一下。

example.en: The receptionist answered the phone on the second ring.
example.zh: 接待人員在第二聲鈴響時接起電話。

example.en: Please ask the operator to connect you to my office.
example.zh: 請請總機幫你轉接到我的辦公室。

example.en: Our client called to change the delivery date.
example.zh: 我們的客戶打來要更改交貨日期。

derived.link: call 是基礎字；call + -er，做這件事的人，像 teacher、worker

extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於服裝規定（casual dress）、非正式聚會與對話，語氣輕鬆。也可指臨時性的工作，如 casual worker。

example.en: Our office has casual Friday, so jeans are allowed.
example.zh: 我們辦公室有週五便服日，所以可以穿牛仔褲。

example.en: Casual dress is fine for the training day.
example.zh: 訓練日穿休閒服裝就可以。

example.en: We had a casual conversation before the meeting began.
example.zh: 會議開始前，我們輕鬆聊了一下。

examples.en: You may wear casual clothes to the picnic on Saturday.
examples.zh: 你可以穿休閒服去星期六的野餐。

examples.en: The interview was friendlier and more casual than I expected.
examples.zh: 這場面試比我想的更友善、更輕鬆。

examples.en: Let's have a casual lunch with the new team members.
examples.zh: 我們和新團隊成員一起吃頓輕鬆的午餐吧。

confusable.diff: 拼法相近，causal 是「因果的」，不是「隨意的」。

example.en: The report shows a causal link between price and sales.
example.zh: 報告顯示價格與銷售之間有因果關係。

similar.diff: informal 強調「不正式」；casual 更強調輕鬆、隨意的感覺。

example.en: We held an informal meeting over coffee.
example.zh: 我們邊喝咖啡邊開了一場非正式會議。

example.en: A formal dress code applies to the awards dinner.
example.zh: 頒獎晚宴有正式的服裝規定。

example.en: These shoes are comfortable for a long day at work.
example.zh: 這雙鞋讓你整天上班都很舒服。

example.en: The manager keeps a relaxed style in team meetings.
example.zh: 經理在團隊會議上保持輕鬆的風格。

example.en: The store sells casual shirts and comfortable pants.
example.zh: 這家店賣休閒襯衫和舒適的長褲。

senses.distinguish: 形容聚會、對話、態度時，指輕鬆隨意，不是服裝。

example.en: The CEO gave a casual talk to new employees.
example.zh: 執行長對新進員工做了一場輕鬆的談話。

senses.en: working only when needed, not full time
senses.distinguish: 後面接 worker、staff、job 時，指臨時或不固定的工作。

example.en: The shop hires casual staff in the busy season.
example.zh: 這家店在旺季會雇用臨時人員。

extra_vocab.en: the person who leads a meeting or a group
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於會議、董事會與委員會，指負責主持的人。這個字不分性別，現代商務英文常用它代替 chairman。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: chairperson 不分性別，常可縮短成 chair，如 Please address the chair。

example.en: All chairpersons must submit their reports by Friday noon.
example.zh: 所有主席都必須在星期五中午前交報告。

example.en: He serves as chairperson of the board of our company.
example.zh: 他擔任我們公司的董事長。

example.en: The committee will elect a chairperson at the next meeting.
example.zh: 委員會將在下次會議選出主席。

example.en: The committee chairperson asked everyone to keep comments short.
example.zh: 委員會主席請大家發言簡短一點。

examples.en: The chairperson opened the meeting at nine sharp.
examples.zh: 主席九點整準時開會。

examples.en: A new chairperson will be chosen at the annual meeting.
examples.zh: 新的主席將在年度會議上選出。

examples.en: Please send your questions to the chairperson in advance.
examples.zh: 請事先把你的問題寄給主席。

examples.en: She became chairperson of the company at the age of forty.
examples.zh: 她在四十歲時成為公司的主席。

similar.diff: chairman 是較傳統的說法，字面指男性；現在多改用 chairperson。

example.en: The chairman thanked everyone for coming to the meeting.
example.zh: 主席感謝大家出席這場會議。

similar.diff: chair 是 chairperson 的簡短說法，口語與會議中很常用。

example.en: The chair asked each member to speak for two minutes.
example.zh: 主席請每位成員發言兩分鐘。

example.en: The director will join the meeting by video.
example.zh: 董事會透過視訊參加會議。

example.en: The committee meets on the first Monday of each month.
example.zh: 委員會在每月的第一個星期一開會。

example.en: The board approved the plan after a short discussion.
example.zh: 董事會在簡短討論後核准了這項計畫。

derived.link: chair 是基礎字；chair + person，主持會議的人，不分性別
chair + man，主持會議的男性，像 businessman
chair + woman，主持會議的女性，與 chairman 成對

extra_vocab.en: to shout to show you are happy or to support someone
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於活動、慶祝與運動場景，指大聲歡呼或加油。cheer up 則常用在鼓勵、安慰別人的情境。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: cheer up 是片語動詞，受詞是代名詞時要放中間：cheer him up，不說 cheer up him。

example.en: The audience cheers whenever the CEO makes a joke.
example.zh: 每當執行長開玩笑，觀眾都會歡呼。

example.en: The cheers from the crowd could be heard across the street.
example.zh: 對街都聽得到群眾的歡呼聲。

example.en: The staff cheered when the manager announced the bonus.
example.zh: 經理宣布獎金時，員工們歡呼起來。

example.en: Fans were cheering loudly at the end of the game.
example.zh: 比賽結束時，球迷們大聲歡呼。

example.en: A short break might cheer you up after the long meeting.
example.zh: 開完長會後休息一下可能會讓你好一些。

example.en: We will cheer for our team at the sports day.
example.zh: 運動日當天我們會為我們的隊伍加油。

example.en: Colleagues gathered along the road to cheer on the marathon runners.
example.zh: 同事們聚在路邊為馬拉松跑者加油。

examples.en: The crowd began to cheer when the winner walked on stage.
examples.zh: 得獎者走上舞台時，群眾開始歡呼。

examples.en: A small gift can cheer up a tired coworker.
examples.zh: 一份小禮物可以讓疲累的同事振作起來。

examples.en: Everyone raised a glass and shouted cheers after the speech.
examples.zh: 演講結束後，大家舉杯喊乾杯。

confusable.diff: 發音相近，但 chair 是「椅子」或「主席」，cheer 是「歡呼」。

example.en: Please take a chair near the front of the room.
example.zh: 請在房間前面找一張椅子坐下。

similar.diff: applaud 強調鼓掌；cheer 強調大聲歡呼、喊叫。

example.en: The audience stood up to applaud the speaker.
example.zh: 觀眾起立為演講者鼓掌。

example.en: We will celebrate the product launch on Friday evening.
example.zh: 我們會在星期五晚上慶祝新產品上市。

example.en: The manager encourages staff to share new ideas.
example.zh: 經理鼓勵員工分享新點子。

example.en: Staff came to cheer at the company sports day.
example.zh: 員工來到公司運動日為大家加油。

example.en: A loud cheer rose when the results were announced.
example.zh: 宣布結果時，響起一陣大聲的歡呼。

senses.en: to shout to show you are happy or to support someone

example.en: Our staff came to cheer for the company team.
example.zh: 我們的員工來為公司的隊伍加油。

senses.distinguish: 常和 up 連用，如 cheer up；後面接人，指鼓勵對方。

example.en: The good news cheered the whole team after a hard week.
example.zh: 辛苦的一週後，這個好消息讓整個團隊高興起來。

extra_vocab.en: cold enough to make you feel uncomfortable
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於天氣預報、出差與旅遊情境，指稍冷、讓人想多穿衣服的程度。也可比喻對方態度冷淡。

example.en: Tomorrow will be chillier, so please dress warmly for the trip.
example.zh: 明天會更冷，所以旅行請穿暖一點。

example.en: January is usually the chilliest month in this part of the country.
example.zh: 一月通常是這個地區最冷的月份。

example.en: The chilly weather kept many customers away from the outdoor market.
example.zh: 寒冷的天氣讓許多顧客不去戶外市集。

example.en: On a chilly morning, the staff arrived early to set up.
example.zh: 在一個寒冷的早晨，員工們提早到場布置。

example.en: The proposal got a chilly reception from the board.
example.zh: 這項提案受到董事會的冷淡回應。

examples.en: It was chilly in Seattle, so I wore a coat.
examples.zh: 西雅圖很冷，所以我穿了外套。

examples.en: The meeting room is chilly because the air conditioning is strong.
examples.zh: 會議室很冷，因為冷氣很強。

examples.en: The forecast says it will be chilly this weekend.
examples.zh: 預報說這個週末會很冷。

confusable.diff: 發音完全相同，但 chili 是「辣椒」或辣味燉菜，和天氣冷無關。

example.en: The restaurant is famous for its chili soup.
example.zh: 這家餐廳以辣椒湯聞名。

similar.diff: cold 是一般的「冷」，程度可以更強；chilly 是稍冷、讓人不太舒服。

example.en: It is cold in the warehouse, so wear gloves.
example.zh: 倉庫裡很冷，所以要戴手套。

similar.diff: cool 是涼爽、通常讓人舒服；chilly 涼到有點不舒服。

example.en: The cool air made the office comfortable.
example.zh: 涼爽的空氣讓辦公室很舒服。

example.en: It was freezing outside, so we stayed in the lobby.
example.zh: 外面冷得要命，所以我們待在大廳。

example.en: Please bring a warm jacket for the evening tour.
example.zh: 晚間的導覽請帶一件保暖外套。

derived.link: chill 是基礎字；chill + -y，變成形容詞「冷颼颼的」，像 windy、rainy

example.en: Please bring a warm coat because the hall is chilly.
example.zh: 請帶一件保暖外套，因為大廳很冷。

senses.distinguish: 後面接 reception、greeting、look 等字時，指態度冷淡，不是天氣。

example.en: The two managers gave each other a chilly greeting.
example.zh: 兩位經理冷淡地向彼此打了招呼。

extra_vocab.en: a person who works at a desk or counter and helps customers or keeps records
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於商店、銀行、飯店與辦公室，指櫃台人員或文書人員。美式發音是 /klɜːrk/，不要唸成 /klerk/。

example.en: Two clerks were sorting the documents at the end of the hall.
example.zh: 兩位職員正在走廊盡頭整理文件。

example.en: A sales clerk helped me find the right size.
example.zh: 一位銷售店員幫我找到合適的尺寸。

example.en: The front desk clerk called a taxi for the guests.
example.zh: 櫃台人員為客人叫了計程車。

example.en: We are hiring a file clerk to organize our records.
example.zh: 我們正在徵一位檔案管理員來整理我們的紀錄。

examples.en: The clerk checked the price and put the items in a bag.
examples.zh: 店員確認價格後，把商品放進袋子。

examples.en: The bank clerk asked me to fill out another form.
examples.zh: 銀行行員請我再填一張表格。

examples.en: A clerk will enter the data into the system today.
examples.zh: 今天會有一位職員把資料輸入系統。

examples.en: The postal clerk weighed the package and gave me a receipt.
examples.zh: 郵局人員秤了包裹重量，並給我一張收據。

similar.diff: cashier 專指負責收錢結帳的人；clerk 的範圍更廣。

example.en: The cashier gave me change and a receipt.
example.zh: 收銀員找錢給我，並給了我收據。

similar.diff: assistant 是協助上司或專業人員的助理；clerk 偏向櫃台或文書工作。

example.en: The office assistant will send you the form today.
example.zh: 辦公室助理今天會把表格寄給你。

example.en: The cashier asked if we wanted a bag.
example.zh: 收銀員問我們要不要袋子。

example.en: My assistant will book the meeting room for you.
example.zh: 我的助理會幫你預約會議室。

example.en: The receptionist greeted every visitor with a smile.
example.zh: 接待人員笑著問候每位訪客。

derived.link: clerk 的形容詞形式，指文書、事務工作，像 medical 的字尾 -ical

senses.en: a person who helps customers at a store, bank, or hotel desk

example.en: The hotel clerk gave us two keys for the room.
example.zh: 飯店櫃台人員給了我們兩把房間鑰匙。

senses.en: a person who does office work such as filing and entering data
senses.distinguish: 後面接 file、office、records 等字，或在辦公室工作時，指文書事務人員。

example.en: The office clerk files all the invoices every Friday.
example.zh: 辦公室職員每週五整理所有發票。

extra_vocab.en: the movement of something around, or the number of copies of a newspaper sold
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於報章雜誌的發行量、空氣或血液循環，以及文件傳閱。要從上下文判斷是哪一個意思。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 表示發行量時常用 a circulation of + 數字，後面常接 copies。

example.en: Newspaper circulation has dropped as more people read online news.
example.zh: 越來越多人讀網路新聞，報紙發行量下降了。

example.en: Open the windows to improve air circulation in the room.
example.zh: 打開窗戶可以改善房間的空氣流通。

example.en: Many old banknotes are still in circulation today.
example.zh: 許多舊鈔票至今仍在流通。

examples.en: The magazine has a circulation of over two hundred thousand copies.
examples.zh: 這本雜誌的發行量超過二十萬本。

examples.en: Regular walking after lunch can improve your blood circulation.
examples.zh: 午餐後規律散步可以改善血液循環。

examples.en: Please check the circulation list before you send the memo.
examples.zh: 寄出備忘錄前，請先確認傳閱名單。

similar.diff: distribution 指把東西分發出去；circulation 指流動、傳閱或發行的數量。

example.en: The distribution of the new catalog begins on Monday.
example.zh: 新型錄的分發從星期一開始。

example.en: The magazine comes out on the first day of each month.
example.zh: 這本雜誌每月一號出刊。

example.en: Our company pays for a yearly subscription to this journal.
example.zh: 我們公司為這本期刊支付年度訂閱費。

example.en: Please send me a copy of the final report.
example.zh: 請寄一份最終報告給我。

derived.link: circulate 是基礎字；circulate + -ion，動詞變名詞，像 educate → education
和 circle（圓）同一詞幹，circular 是形容詞「圓形的」，也可當名詞「傳單」

senses.en: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold

example.en: The paper's circulation grew by ten percent last year.
example.zh: 這份報紙的發行量去年成長了百分之十。

senses.en: the movement of air, blood, or water around a place or body
senses.distinguish: 後面接 air、blood 等字時，指流動循環，不是報章雜誌。

example.en: Poor circulation in the warehouse makes the air feel heavy.
example.zh: 倉庫的空氣流通不良，讓人覺得空氣很悶。

senses.en: the passing of money or papers from person to person
senses.distinguish: 和 money、notes、documents 一起出現時，指在人與人之間傳遞流通。

example.en: The draft was kept in limited circulation among senior managers.
example.zh: 這份草案只在高階主管之間有限傳閱。

extra_vocab.en: lasting for a long time or happening again and again
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於醫療、保險、人力與經濟新聞，指長期存在、很難解決的問題，如 chronic shortage。語氣偏負面。

example.en: Our health plan also covers treatment for chronic illness.
example.zh: 我們的健康保險也涵蓋慢性病的治療。

example.en: The hospital suffers from a chronic shortage of nurses.
example.zh: 這家醫院長期缺乏護理師。

example.en: Late deliveries are a chronic problem for this supplier.
example.zh: 延遲交貨是這家供應商的長期問題。

examples.en: Chronic back pain is a common reason for missing work.
examples.zh: 慢性背痛是請假不上班的常見原因。

examples.en: Some insurance plans do not cover chronic conditions.
examples.zh: 有些保險方案不涵蓋慢性疾病。

examples.en: The region has struggled with chronic unemployment for years.
examples.zh: 這個地區多年來一直為長期失業所苦。

examples.en: Chronic lateness can hurt your chances of getting a promotion.
examples.zh: 經常遲到可能會影響你升遷的機會。

confusable.diff: acute 是「急性的、突發嚴重的」；chronic 是「慢性的、長期的」，兩者常成對比較。

example.en: The doctor said it was an acute problem and needed quick treatment.
example.zh: 醫生說這是急性問題，需要盡快治療。

similar.diff: long-term 只說明時間長，語氣中性；chronic 常帶有難以解決的負面感。

example.en: We signed a long-term contract with the new supplier.
example.zh: 我們和新供應商簽了長期合約。

similar.diff: persistent 強調一直持續、不消失；chronic 多用於疾病或長期問題。

example.en: Persistent noise in the office makes it hard to focus.
example.zh: 辦公室裡持續不斷的噪音讓人很難專心。

example.en: She took two weeks off because of a serious illness.
example.zh: 她因為重病請了兩週的假。

example.en: The clinic offers free tests for heart disease.
example.zh: 這間診所提供免費的心臟病檢查。

senses.en: lasting a long time and hard to cure, used for illnesses

example.en: Chronic headaches made it hard for him to work full time.
example.zh: 慢性頭痛讓他很難全職工作。

senses.en: continuing for a long time and hard to fix, used for problems
senses.distinguish: 後面接 shortage、delay、debt 等非醫療的字時，指長期存在的問題。

example.en: Chronic delays at the port have raised our shipping costs.
example.zh: 港口長期的延誤提高了我們的運費。
